title: Isolation of adult mouse microglia using their in vitro adherent properties
protocol: Euthanize adult C57/BL6J mouse via cervical dislocation.
Immerse the head in 80% ethanol for sterilization.
Remove skin and skull using sterile dissection tools.
Place the brain into a petri dish containing ice-cold (4°C) dissection media.
Carefully remove meninges using sharp forceps under the dissecting microscope.
Dissect the forebrain region of interest from the brain, removing mid- and hind-brain as well as the hippocampus.
Dissociate the tissue via mechanical and enzymatic dissociation.
Filter the dissociated tissue.
Re-suspend the tissue-containing media into a flask.
Place the tissue into a pre-weighed falcon tube containing ice cold HBSS and record the weight of the tissue.
Transfer the tissue to a sterile petri dish and wash with ice cold HBSS.
Dice the tissue into small cubes less than 1 mm³ using a sterile scalpel.
Add enzyme digestion mixture to the diced tissue in the petri-dish, collecting the media containing tissue fragments and transferring this to a sterile Falcon tube.
Incubate for 15 minutes at 37°C while applying gentle agitation.
Triturate the mixture approximately 10 times.
Re-incubate for an additional 15 minutes at 37°C with gentle rotation.
Triturate the mixture a further approximately 10 times.
Allow undigested tissue to settle.
Collect 5 mL of tissue-containing media at a time through a sterile 70 μm Nylon mesh filter into a sterile 50 mL Falcon tube.
Pass an additional 10 mL of warm complete media through the filter for rinsing, making a final volume of 20 mL per 1 g of tissue.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 170 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant by gentle pipetting.
Re-suspend cells in 10 or 15 mL of complete media and transfer into a non-coated T25 or T75 tissue culture flask, respectively.
Incubate cells at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Isolate microglia by repeated tapping to remove non-adherent cells.
Check the T25 or T75 flask for adherent adult mouse microglia using a bright field microscope.
Perform 1–2 full media changes in the flask with warmed complete media before observing microglial adherence if debris is present.
Tap the flask firmly and repeatedly to dissociate non-microglial cells.
Check for any adherent cells which are not microglia under the microscope.
Remove all media containing floating non-adherent cells, discard, and replace with fresh, warmed complete media.
Repeat washing steps until only phase bright microglia appear, with all cells adherent to the bottom of the flask.
Incubate pure microglia cultures for 2–5 days in fresh complete media at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Observe microglia under the microscope after 2 days to assess morphology before harvesting.
Harvest microglia if they have spread out into rod-like and ramified morphologies.
Remove all media from T25 or T75 flask.
Add 1 mL (T25) or 3 mL (T75) of 0.5% Trypsin-EDTA (warmed to 37°C).
Incubate for 2 min at 37°C.
Repeatedly firmly tap flask to aid in microglial detachment.
Observe microglial detachment under the microscope.
If all microglia appear detached, proceed to next step.
Use a sterile rubber cell scraper to gently pass over the bottom of the flask if necessary.
Pass the scraper over an additional time to detach adherent cells.
Add 4 mL (T25) or 7 mL (T75) of complete media to stop the Trypsin-EDTA reaction.
Collect the 5 or 10 mL media containing the microglial cell suspension and transfer to a sterile falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 170 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Re-suspend the cell pellet.
Cells can be counted at this point.
Plate cells in 96, 48, 24 or 6 well plates without poly-D-lysine (PDL) or matrigel coating due to their adherent properties.
Recommend plating in 48 well plates for functional assays at a density between 1.6 × 10^4 and 3.2 × 10^4 cells/cm².
Note: Isolated adult mouse microglia have a limited proliferative capacity in vitro with approximately 5.5% Edu+ microglia present over 48 hours.
Cells cannot be passaged or re-plated but can remain in culture for 1–2 weeks depending on the purity of the original culture.
